title: HOPPER: A Hop-by-hop Entanglement Distribution Protocol for Asynchronous Quantum Networks
summary: The quantum Internet relies on the ability to distribute entangled quantum bits (ebits) between quantum memories at the end nodes, to perform applications like blind or distributed quantum computing that are impossible if end nodes are connected via a classical, i.e., non-quantum network. This need creates new challenges due to the fragile nature of entanglement, which decoheres over short timescales and cannot be amplified, buffered, or retransmitted.
